name: Hamutal
title: Mother of two kings of Judah
summary: Hamutal was the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah and wife to King Josiah of Judah. She was mother to two kings: Jehoahaz (Shallum) and Zedekiah, who both reigned over Judah in the kingdom's final and most turbulent years before the Babylonian exile.

keyEvents.title: Marriage to King Josiah
keyEvents.description: Hamutal married King Josiah of Judah. She was one of his wives and became the mother of two of his sons who later became kings.

keyEvents.title: Her son Jehoahaz becomes king
keyEvents.description: After Josiah's death at the battle of Megiddo, Hamutal's son Jehoahaz (also called Shallum) was anointed king over Judah by the people of the land. He reigned for only three months.

keyEvents.title: Jehoahaz deposed by Pharaoh Neco
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh Necho of Egypt deposed Jehoahaz and took him into captivity in Egypt, where he died. This was a great loss for Hamutal, who lost her son to exile.

keyEvents.title: Zedekiah, the Son, Appointed King
keyEvents.description: Hamutal's other son Mattaniah was appointed king by Nebuchadnezzar and given the name Zedekiah. He became Judah's last king and reigned for eleven years.

keyEvents.title: The Fall of Jerusalem and Zedekiah's Fate
keyEvents.description: Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon, leading to the siege and destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BC. Zedekiah was captured, his sons were killed before his eyes, he was blinded, and taken to Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Hamutal's Exile to Babylon
keyEvents.description: According to Jeremiah, the king's mother (Hamutal) was taken into exile in Babylon along with the other captives after the fall of Jerusalem, marking the end of the Davidic monarchy in Judah.
